items.q: If Sam is shorter than Tina and Tina is shorter than Uma, who is the tallest?
items.answer: Uma. Putting the statements in order (shorter first): Sam > Tina > Uma.

items.q: If the light is red, cars stop. The cars did not stop. Was the light red?
items.answer: No. The rule says: If the light is red, cars stop. “cars stop” is false here, so “the light is red” must be false too — otherwise the rule would have made it true. (That's modus tollens: if the result didn't happen, the condition can't have either.)

items.q: If you heat ice, it melts. The ice melted. Was it heated?
items.answer: Not necessarily. The rule (If you heat ice, it melts) says the first part guarantees the second — not the other way round. It melts could have other causes, so it doesn't prove that you heat ice. (Concluding it would be the fallacy of affirming the consequent.)

items.q: All squares are rectangles. All rectangles are shapes. Are all squares shapes?
items.answer: Yes. Every squar is a rectangl, and every rectangl is a shap, so every squar is a shap.

items.q: What comes next: 1, 4, 9, 16?

items.q: A book and a bookmark cost $5.50 together. The book costs $5.00 more than the bookmark. How much does the bookmark cost?
items.answer: $0.25 (25 cents). Writing what's stated as equations: A book + a bookmark = 5.50; The book = the bookmark + 5.00. Solving them together gives book = 5.25, bookmark = 0.25.

items.q: Liam has 3 times as many cards as Noah. Noah has 7 cards. How many cards does Liam have?
items.answer: 21. Writing what's stated as equations: Liam = 3 × Noah; Noah = 7. Solving them together gives Liam = 21, Noah = 7.
